event: Gilt market crisis after the September mini-budget: LDI pension funds forced to sell, 30-year yields up 130 basis points in three trading days; the Bank of England buys long gilts to restore order (£19.3bn bought by 14 October).
Fitch downgrades the US from AAA to AA+, citing fiscal deterioration and repeated debt-limit standoffs.
Weak 30-year bond auction: the issue tails by about 5 basis points (4.769% against 4.716% when-issued) and dealers take about a quarter, twice their usual share; part of the 2023 term-premium spike.
Moody's cuts China's outlook to negative, citing support for indebted local governments and state firms.
Fitch cuts China's outlook to negative on rising government debt and risks to public finances.
30-year gilt yield reaches its highest since 1998 (about 5.3%) and keeps rising for two more days; sterling falls at the same time, a sign of fiscal rather than growth worry.
Treasury sell-off after the April tariff announcements: the 10-year yield rises about half a point in a week to 4.49%, the biggest weekly jump since 2001, while the dollar falls.
Moody's downgrades the US from Aaa to Aa1, the last of the three big agencies to drop the top rating.
20-year bond auction tails by about 1 basis point at above 5% (5.047% against 5.035% when-issued); long yields jump the same day.
30-year gilt yield reaches about 5.7%, the highest since 1998, ahead of the autumn Budget.
